newsitem.title: USA: Cincinnati Microwave files for Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Cincinnati Microwave files for Chapter 11.

text.p: Cincinnati Microwave Inc. said Friday it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, allowing it to reorganize its operations or to liquidate its assets.

The company, which makes ultrahigh frequency and microwave wireless communications products, warned Thursday it might take the action and said it called off its merger agreement with BEL-Tronics USA Inc.
"Our efforts to find partners, or sell portions of the business in order to generate enough cash to carry the company forward have been unsuccessful," Chief Executive Erika Williams said.

"The $10 million in excess inventory purchased in 1995 and the outstanding shareholder lawsuit have hindered our ability to attract suitable partners. We expect several interested parties to bid for portions of the company's assets under court protection."
The action was filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Southern Ohio-Western Division.
Cincinnati Microwave's stock was unchanged at 37.5 cents on Nasdaq at mid-afternoon.
